key_insight: Research-agent benchmarks can overestimate real-world ability when they ignore prior session decisions and the state of unfinished project workspaces.
engineering_relevance: Reliable research agents must satisfy the current request while preserving historical constraints and working correctly with existing project artifacts.
method: Build 75 tasks from recruited researchers’ real agent sessions and full project workspaces.
Replay each workspace to a real request boundary without cleanup, retaining earlier artifacts and summarizing still-active requests.
Evaluate with intent-aligned binary checklists that credit any valid solution.
evidence_signal: Across seven frontier models and 1,173 checklist items, the strongest model fully passed 66.2% of tasks; three models’ roughly 69% pass rates on delivery contracts and general norms fell to 28.4–40.0% when contextual requirements were included.
watch_item: The 75-task sample may not capture the full diversity of research workflows, so generalization beyond the sampled projects remains uncertain.
paper_title: ARE-bench: Benchmarking Agents' Research Ability in Real-World Researcher Sessions and Workspaces
